950:
(a) Definitions used in the Georgia Comprehensive Solid Waste Management Act, as may be amended from time to time (O.C.G.A. § 12-8-20 et seq.), and the Georgia Hazardous Waste Management Act, as may be amended from time to time (O.C.G.A. § 12-8-60 et seq.), are specifically incorporated in this section by reference, to the extent that they are relevant and appropriate to the context in which they may be used in this article.
(b) The following words, terms and phrases, when used in this article, shall have the meanings ascribed to them in this subsection, except where context clearly indicates a different meaning:
Board means the board of commissioners of the county.
Bulky waste means a type of solid waste that by weight or volume exceeds the designated capacity of solid waste storage or collection containers. The term "bulky waste" shall include, without limitation, appliances, furniture, crates, corrugated cardboard and other similar items. The term "bulky waste" shall not include yard debris, tires or other solid waste requiring special handling under state law.
Commercial solid waste means a type of solid waste generated by stores, offices, restaurants, warehouses and other nonmanufacturing activities. The term "commercial solid waste" includes solid waste generated by premises having three or more residential dwelling units on the premises such as apartment buildings, condominiums and mobile home parks. The term "commercial solid waste" does not include other residential wastes, industrial wastes or construction and demolition waste.
Composting means solid waste handling which consists of the controlled biological decomposition of organic matter into a stable, odor-free humus.
Construction and demolition waste means a type of solid waste that is generally considered to be not water soluble and nonhazardous in nature, including, but not limited to, building materials and rubble resulting from construction, remodeling, repair and demolition operations on pavements, houses, commercial buildings and other structures. Such waste includes but is not limited to steel, glass, brick, concrete, asphalt roofing material, pipe, gypsum wallboard, lumber, inert debris and other nonputrescible waste which has a low potential for ground water contamination. Such waste does not include any municipal or agricultural solid waste. Mixing of construction or demolition waste with other types of solid waste, including material from a construction or demolition site which is not from the actual construction or demolition of a structure, will cause it to be classified as other than construction or demolition waste.
Containerized waste means solid waste (other than that which requires special handling) which is placed in cans, plastic garbage bags or bulk containers or in bundles, as in the case of bundled yard debris.
County solid waste management system (CSWMS) means the aggregate of those solid waste management facilities owned by, operated under contract with, or operated pursuant to licenses and permits issued by the county.
Curbside means the area between the sidewalk and the street edge or, in areas without sidewalks, the area between the edge of the traveled portion of any public or private street and the property line, which area shall not exceed ten feet. However, the term "curbside" shall also denote and include any other permissible areas on a property where solid waste is regularly placed or deposited for collection, such as, for example, by a garage door.
Customer means a person who uses the solid waste or recycling collection services of a permitted solid waste collector or the appropriate governmental agency or who uses solid waste or recycling disposal facilities, whether publicly or privately owned, located in the county.
Department means the county department of sanitation.
Designated recovered/recyclable material collection location means the location or locations where the owner of the recyclable material places such material for the purpose of materials recovery and recycling, including curbside and recovered material storage containers.
Disposal facility means any facility or location where the disposition of solid waste occurs and includes, but is not limited to, landfills, transfer stations and solid waste thermal treatment technology facilities.
Disposal operation means the performance of solid waste disposal and includes the administration, personnel, land, equipment, design and other elements necessary or used in the work of solid waste disposal.
Garbage means a type of solid waste that includes any accumulation of animal, fruit or vegetable matter that attends the preparation, use, cooking and dealing in, or storage of, edibles, and any other matter of any nature whatsoever, which is putrescible, subject to decay, and/or the generation of noxious or offensive gases or odors, which during or after decay, may serve as breeding or feeding material for flies or other germ carrying insects, rodents or other pests.
Hazardous waste means any solid waste which, because of its quantity, concentration or physical, chemical or infectious characteristics, when improperly transported, disposed of, stored, treated or otherwise managed, may cause or significantly contribute to an increase in mortality, or an increase in serious or incapacitating illness, or may pose a substantial present or potential hazard to human health or the environment when improperly transported, disposed of, stored, treated or otherwise managed. Hazardous waste also includes those solid wastes defined as hazardous by any federal law, rule or regulation and/or by the Georgia Hazardous Waste Management Act, O.C.G.A. § 12-8-60 et seq., or in regulations promulgated by the state department of natural resources, chapter 391-3-11, as may be amended from time to time.
Industrial solid waste means solid waste generated by manufacturing or industrial processes that is not a hazardous waste as defined in this section or by the Georgia Hazardous Waste Management Act, O.C.G.A. § 12-8-60 et seq., or in regulations promulgated by the state department of natural resources as may be amended from time to time.
Inert debris means land clearing debris, such as stumps, limbs, leaves and brush, as well as concrete, cured asphalt, brick, rock and earth and earth-like products which are not likely to cause production of leachate of environmental concern.
Inert waste landfill means a disposal facility accepting only inert debris that will not or is not likely to cause production of leachate of environmental concern.
Institutional solid waste means municipal solid waste generated by educational, health care and research facilities, including but not limited to schools, hospitals, nursing homes, laboratories and similar establishments.
Landfill means an area of land on which, or an excavation in which, solid waste is placed for permanent disposal and which is not a land application unit, surface impoundment, injection well or compost pile.
Leachate collection system means a system at a landfill for collection of the leachate which may percolate through the waste and into the soils surrounding the landfills.
Litter means all discarded material of every kind and description which, when thrown or deposited in a manner as prohibited by this article, tends to create an eyesore and a danger to public health, safety and well-being. The term "litter" includes all uncontrolled, uncontainerized solid waste.
Materials recovery facility means a solid waste handling facility that provides for the extraction from solid waste of recoverable/recyclable material, material suitable for use as fuel or soil amendment, or any combination of such material.
Municipal solid waste means any solid waste derived from households, including garbage, trash and sanitary waste in septic tanks, and includes solid waste from single-family and multifamily residences, hotels and motels, bunkhouses, campgrounds, picnic grounds and day use recreation areas. The term "municipal solid waste" includes yard trimmings, commercial solid waste and institutional solid waste, but does not include solid waste from mining, agricultural or silvicultural operations or industrial processes or operations.
Municipal solid waste disposal facility means any facility or location where the deposition of any amount of municipal solid waste occurs, including but not limited to municipal solid waste landfills.
Municipal solid waste landfill means a disposal facility, either privately or publicly owned, where any amount of municipal solid waste, whether or not mixed with or including commercial waste, industrial waste, construction and demolition waste, inert debris, nonhazardous sludge or small quantity generator hazardous waste, is disposed of by means of landfilling or burial and then placing an approved cover thereon.
Nuisance means:
(1) Anything which satisfies that definition of the term as defined by O.C.G.A. § 41-1-1 as it maybe amended; or
(2) Anything which occurs during or as a result of the handling or disposal of solid waste to the detriment of the public welfare in that it injures health, offends the senses, obstructs the reasonable and comfortable use of property, or causes inconvenience or discomfort to a community or neighborhood;
(3) Any of the following conditions:
a. Toilets, plumbing, sewers, septic tank systems, containers or any other sanitary waste disposal facility in active failure or visibly in need of repair.
b. Conditions causing the breeding and attraction of rodents, flies, ticks, mosquitoes or any other disease carrying insects, including discarded accumulations of trash, garbage and/or litter.
c. Sewage, kitchen waste discharge, laundry waste discharge, or any other wastes deposited upon or allowed to remain upon the ground's surface or any other place so as to be or to become detrimental to human health or well-being.
d. The keeping of animals or fowl in such a manner as to permit the visible accumulation of excrement.
Subsections (3)(b) and (3)(d) of this definition shall have no application to active farming operations on property zoned agricultural, including active poultry and cattle farms.
Offal waste means a type of solid waste which denotes animal matter, whether of land or marine origin, generated by the processing, preparation or packaging of food or animal matter at butcher shops; slaughterhouses; and/or food processing, packaging, rendering or fertilizer plants.
Owner of recovered recyclable material means the generator of recovered material or its authorized agent, contractor, the recovered material collector, the private recycler, the person having possession of recovered material, or the person to whom the generator has transferred title to the recovered material. The owner shall be deemed to have transferred title to the material at the earliest to occur of (i) when the material is placed or deposited in any curbside storage container or recovered material collection container owned by someone other than the generator of the material for the purpose of recycling, or (ii) the time the collector, recycler, or other person takes possession of the material.
Private industry solid waste facility means a disposal facility which is operated exclusively by and for a private solid waste generator for the purpose of accepting solid waste generated exclusively by the private solid waste generator.
Putrescible waste means solid waste that is capable of being quickly decomposed by microorganisms at ambient temperature and conditions and usually associated with offensive odors and disease vectors. Examples include, but are not limited to, kitchen waste, animal manure, offal waste, dead animals, garbage and other solid waste contaminated by such waste.
Recovered/recyclable material means that material which has a known use, reuse, or recycling potential; can be feasibly used, reused or recycled; and has been diverted or removed from the solid waste stream for sale, use, reuse or recycling whether or not requiring subsequent separation and processing. Such material, once recovered, is not solid waste, but all byproducts of such recovery process which are not recovered material shall remain solid waste.
Recovered/recyclable material collector means a person engaged in the business of separating recovered material, with or without compensation, from residential, business, industrial, commercial, institutional or other similar premises, including persons under contractor agreement with the owner or generator of solid waste, recovered material for collection.
Recycling means any process by which material which would otherwise become solid waste is collected, separated or processed and reused or returned to use in the form of raw materials or products.
Residential collection service means the collection and transportation of recyclable material, yard trash, and other solid waste from residential property by a contractor to a solid waste management facility.
Residential solid waste means any garbage, rubbish, yard trash or bulk item that is usual to housekeeping. Residential solid waste is solid waste generated by the customer at the dwelling unit at which the residential solid waste is collected and does not include items defined in this section as commercially generated waste or exempt waste.
Rubbish means waste material other than garbage, usually attendant to domestic households or housekeeping, attendant to the operation of stores, offices, and other business places. Rubbish is nonputrescible and includes but is not limited to, paper, magazines, packaging, receptacles, textile materials, bottles, cans, and ceramic material.
Solid waste means discarded putrescible and nonputrescible wastes, except water-carried body waste and recovered material, and shall include garbage, rubbish, ashes, street refuse, dead animals, sewage sludge, animal manure, industrial waste, residue from solid waste thermal treatment technology, food processing waste, demolition waste, yard trimmings, inert debris, abandoned automobiles, dredging waste, construction and demolition waste, and other waste material in a solid or semisolid or liquid state not otherwise defined in this section or by O.C.G.A. § 12-8-20 et seq. The term "solid waste" shall not include any materials regulated under the Georgia Water Quality Control Act, O.C.G.A. § 12-5-20 et seq., or the Georgia Air Quality Act of 1978, O.C.G.A. § 12-9-1 et seq. Solid waste includes, but is not limited to, commercial solid waste, construction and demolition waste, containerized and uncontainerized waste, garbage, hazardous waste, industrial solid waste, inert debris, institutional solid waste, municipal solid waste, offal waste, putrescible waste, residential solid waste, rubbish, special wastes, white goods waste and yard trimmings or yard trash. Recovered materials are not solid waste.
Solid waste collector means a person permitted by or, in the case of noncounty businesses, registered with, the county to engage in the business of the collection or transportation of solid waste, but excluding a private citizen who collects or transports solid waste from his own dwelling or residence only or any person who picks up litter.
Solid waste management costs means costs incurred to provide solid waste management services, including, without limitation:
(1) The cost for construction, reconstruction or completion of any facility;
(2) The cost of acquisition or purchase of any facility;
(3) The cost of labor, materials, machinery and equipment;
(4) The cost of fuel, parts, supplies, maintenance, repairs and utilities;
(5) The cost of computer services, data processing and communications;
(6) The cost of all lands and interest therein, leases, property rights, easements and franchises of any nature whatsoever;
(7) The cost of any indemnity or surety bonds and premiums for insurance;
(8) The cost of salaries, workers compensation insurance or other employment benefits;
(9) The cost of uniforms, training, travel and per diem;
(10) Amounts necessary to pay redemption premiums or other costs associated with the early retirement of obligations;
(11) The creation of reserve or debt service funds;
(12) Costs and expenses related to the issuance of obligations, all financing charges and any expenses related to the issuance of obligations, all financing charges and any expenses related to any liquidity facility or credit facility;
(13) The cost of construction plans and specifications, surveys and estimates of costs;
(14) The cost of engineering, financial, legal and other professional services;
(15) The costs associated with any inspections required by this article;
(16) The costs associated with the implementation and enforcement of this article;
(17) Fees and charges designated to offset the impact of any solid waste handling facility;
(18) Fees and charges designated to assist in public education efforts for solid waste management and the administration of the comprehensive solid waste management plan; and
(19) Any and all other costs and expenses properly attributable to providing solid waste management in the county.
Solid waste management facility means any solid waste disposal area, volume reduction plant, transfer station, materials recovery facility, or other facility the purpose of which is the disposal, recycling, processing or storage of solid waste.
Solid waste management plan and solid waste management comprehensive plan mean the county ten-year solid waste management plan, as adopted in 1992 and updated in 1998, which sets forth the goals, objectives and polices for solid waste management in the county.
Solid waste thermal treatment technology means any solid waste management facility that reduces the amount of solid waste to be disposed of through a process of combustion, with or without the production of waste energy.
Special wastes means solid wastes that can require special handling and management under federal, state or local laws, including but not limited to, white goods waste, waste tires, used oil, lead-acid batteries, construction and demolition debris, ash residue, yard trimmings and biological wastes.
Transfer station means a solid waste management facility used to transfer solid waste from one transportation vehicle to another for transportation to a disposal facility or other processing operation.
White goods waste means solid waste consisting of discarded or abandoned large appliances, including refrigerators, freezers, stoves, ranges, water heaters and similar domestic or commercial large appliances. The term "white goods waste" does not include material that is recovered material.
Yard trimmings and yard trash mean leaves, brush, grass clippings, shrub and tree prunings, discarded Christmas trees, nursery and greenhouse vegetative residuals and vegetative matter resulting from landscape development and maintenance, other than mining, agricultural and silvicultural operations.
(Ord. No. 84, art. I, pt. 5, 6-28-1999; Amendment A of 11-12-2002, art. I, pt. 5, 11-12-2002)

951:
(a) No person shall engage in solid waste handling, except in such a manner as to conform to and comply with this article and all applicable state and federal legislation, rules, regulations and orders.
(b) No person shall engage in solid waste handling in a manner which will be conducive to insect and rodent infestation or the harboring and feeding of wild dogs or other animals; impair the air quality; impair the quality of the ground or surface waters; or impair the public health, safety or well-being as may be determined by local, state or federal authorities.
(c) No person shall collect and dispose of solid waste for a fee without obtaining authorization to provide service from the county and any other requisite governing authority as required by state or federal law.
(d) No individual, partnership, corporation or other entity shall collect or dispose of construction or demolition debris or inert debris without obtaining an authorization to provide such service from the county and any other requisite governing authority as required by state or federal law.
(e) No solid waste may be disposed of by any person, on property located in the county, in an open dump, nor may any person cause, suffer, allow or permit open dumping on his property as defined by the Rules of the state department of natural resources, environmental protection division, chapter 391-3-4-04.
(f) The owner, occupant, manager or other person in charge of any premises, office, business establishment, institution, industry, or similar facility, including construction or demolition sites, shall be responsible for the collection and transportation of all solid waste accumulated at the premises, office, business establishment, institution, or similar facility to a solid waste disposal facility operating in compliance with the state environmental protection division rules and regulations unless arrangements have been made for such services with a solid waste collector operating in compliance with this article.
(g) No owner, occupant, manager or other person in charge of any premises, place, or facility shall allow the accumulation on premises under his control, or on or about his residential unit or commercial establishment, of solid waste where such solid waste creates or may create a health hazard to any other person, or is unsightly, or emits foul or obnoxious odors which constitute either a public or private nuisance. Such conduct shall constitute a violation of this article. Each day the solid waste remains on the premises may constitute a separate violation of this article and shall subject such owner, occupant, manager or other person to the penalties provided in this article.
(h) No person may dispose of yard trimmings in the county nor dispose of yard trimmings generated in the county unless such disposal is carried out in accordance with section 70-37.
(i) No person shall create, maintain, support, aid or fail to correct any condition declared to be a nuisance as defined in section 70-34.

953:
(a) It shall be unlawful to place or mix yard trimmings with other solid waste within the county.
(b) Yard trimmings shall not be disposed of at any solid waste disposal facility with liners or leachate collection systems or any municipal solid waste landfills which have received a vertical expansion under O.C.G.A. § 12-8-40.2.
(c) Yard trimmings shall be sorted and stored for collection in a manner that facilitates collection, composting, or other lawful handling.
(d) Yard trimmings shall be placed in separate bags or containers. Such bags or containers may include reusable receptacles provided by residents which meet the requirements of this part, watertight paper bags manufactured for yard trimming disposal which, when full, do not exceed 50 pounds in weight, or special containers provided by a solid waste collector, but may not include plastic bags. Notwithstanding the foregoing provisions of this subsection, tree branches, tree trunks, and heavy brush which cannot be containerized and do not exceed four feet in length or six inches in diameter may be neatly stacked. No further preparation shall be required.
(e) Upon collection, yard trimmings shall be sorted and stockpiled until their ultimate disposal by chipping, mulching, other beneficial use, or recycling.
(f) The county manager or his designee is authorized to modify the requirements for preparation of yard trimmings and to arrange collection services for organized community cleanup programs which are coordinated with the county manager or his designee expressly and solely for the cleanup of massive property destruction resulting from fires and natural disasters.
(g) Yard trimmings shall not be placed at the curb of or adjacent to the street in front of any residence, place or premises for more than two weeks. Each day such wastes remain at the curb after the 14th day shall constitute a separate violation of this article. It shall be unlawful for any person to place yard trimmings for removal by any solid waste collector which are not prepared, placed and separated as required by this article.
(h) It shall be the duty of the solid waste collector to notify the county manager or his designee of any noncompliance with this part. Upon such notice of noncompliance, the county manager or his designee shall notify the property owner or occupant in writing to remove all yard trimmings not prepared and placed as required by this section, at the property owner's expense or to prepare them in accordance with this article. Upon the failure of the property owner or occupant to remove or prepare such yard trimmings within the time set forth in the notice, the property owner or occupant shall receive a citation as provided in division 4 of this article.
(Ord. No. 84, art. I, pt. 8, 6-28-1999)

(a) Municipal solid waste landfills.
(1) Permit required. Any person desiring to operate a municipal solid waste landfill within the county must first obtain a written permit to establish and operate the landfill from the board of commissioners. The permit shall be renewable annually and must be obtained prior to the issuance of a business license.
(2) Equipment. All such municipal solid waste landfills shall have adequate equipment on their premises to maintain the facility in accordance with federal, state and local law. All equipment shall be maintained in good working order and shall include a crawler-type tractor with blade bulldozer and an earth scraper with a minimum capacity of eight cubic yards.
(3) Fences. All municipal solid waste landfills shall be enclosed with a fence at least five feet high with openings therein not less than those in two inch mesh wire or some other similar fencing material or device, which shall first be approved by the county manager or his designee. The fencing shall be adequate to prevent paper and similar or related refuse from blowing from the landfill onto adjoining roadways or neighboring property.
(4) Authority of county; revocation of permits. All other phases of the operation of a municipal solid waste landfill not specifically mentioned in this article shall be subject to the approval of the county manager or his designee. Any and all permits to establish and maintain landfills granted under this section shall be subject to revocation in the discretion of the county.
(5) Annual permitting fee. A permitting fee, payable annually, is hereby established for all municipal solid waste landfills within the county's jurisdiction. The annual permit shall be for the purpose of ensuring the landfill meets the applicable rules and regulations as set forth in this article and as set forth by federal and state authorities. A permit shall be issued annually with inspections of the landfills performed weekly at a minimum, and additionally as determined by the county manager or his designee.

(1) Permit required. Any person desiring to operate a construction and demolition landfill within the county must first obtain a written permit to establish and operate the landfill from the board of commissioners. The permit shall be renewable annually and must be obtained prior to the issuance of a business license.
(2) Equipment. All such construction and demolition landfills shall have adequate equipment on their premises to maintain the facility in accordance with federal, state and local law.

All construction and demolition landfills shall be enclosed with a fence at least five feet high with openings therein not less than those in two inch mesh wire or some other similar fencing material or device, which shall first be approved by the county manager or his designee. The annual permit shall be for the purpose of ensuring the landfill meets the applicable rules and regulations as set forth in this article and as set forth by federal and state authorities. A permit shall be issued annually with inspections of the landfills performed weekly at a minimum, and additionally as determined by the county manager or his designee.

All other phases of the operation of an inert waste landfill not specifically mentioned in this article shall be subject to the approval of the county manager or his designee. Any and all permits to establish and maintain landfills granted under this section shall be subject to revocation in the discretion of the county.

The annual permit shall be for the purpose of ensuring the landfill meets the applicable rules and regulations as set forth in this article and as set forth by federal and state authorities. A permit shall be issued annually with inspections of the landfills performed weekly at a minimum, and additionally as determined by the county manager or his designee.
(d) All other solid waste disposal facilities and transfer stations.
(1) Permit required. Any person desiring to operate a solid waste disposal facility or transfer station within the county shall first obtain a written permit from the county manager or his designee. The following words, terms and phrases, when used in this article, shall have the meanings ascribed to them in this section, except where the context clearly indicates a different meaning:
Biomedical waste means:
(1) Pathological waste, which means recognizable human tissues and body parts except teeth which are removed during surgery, obstetrical procedures, autopsy, and laboratory procedures.
(2) Biological waste, which means bulk blood products, exudates, secretions, suctionings, and other bulk body fluids which cannot or are not directly discarded into a county sewer system.
(3) Cultures and stocks of infectious agents and associated biologicals, including cultures from medical and pathological laboratories, cultures and stocks of infectious agents from research and industrial laboratories, wastes from the production of biologicals, discarded live and attenuated vaccines, and culture dishes and devices used to transfer, inoculate, and mix cultures.
(4) Contaminated animal carcasses, body parts, their bedding, and other wastes from such animals which have been exposed to infectious agents, capable of causing disease in man, during research, production of biologicals, or testing of pharmaceuticals.
(5) Sharps, which means any discarded article that may cause punctures or cuts. Such waste includes, but is not limited to, items such as needles, IV tubing and syringes with needles attached, and scalpel blades.
(6) Chemotherapy waste, which means any disposable material which has come in contact with cytotoxic antineoplastic agents (agents toxic to cells) masks, gloves, gowns, empty IV tubing bags and vials, and other contaminated medical materials, parts and equipment.
(7) Discarded medical equipment and parts, not including expendable supplies and materials, which have not been decontaminated, and that were in contact with infectious agents.
Hazardous waste means any solid waste which has been defined as a hazardous waste in regulations promulgated by the state board of natural resources, chapter 391-3-11, and under federal regulations promulgated by the United States Environmental Protection Agency and codified at 40 CFR 261.3.
Incineration means a controlled process by which solid, liquid and gaseous combustible wastes are burned and changed into gases and a residue produced which is relatively free of combustible materials.
Industrial waste means solid waste generated by manufacturing or industrial processes that is not a hazardous waste under regulations promulgated by the state board of natural resources, chapter 391-3-11.
Medical facility means, but is not limited to, clinics, dental offices, funeral homes, health maintenance organizations (HMOs), hospitals, laboratories, medical buildings, physicians offices, veterinary offices, research and manufacturing facilities, nursing homes, and blood banks.
Pyrolysis means the chemical decomposition of a material by heat in the absence of oxygen.

Where rent is paid, charged, billed, or falls due on either a weekly, monthly, or other term basis, only the rent covering the period commencing on December 1, 2024, shall be subject to this tax.
(6) For any occupancy prior to December 1, 2024, tax shall be paid upon such occupancy pursuant to the provisions of chapter 74, article II of the Forsyth County Code of Ordinances in effect at the time of such occupancy.
(Ord. No. 86-C, § 1(Exh. A), 10-3-2024)
996:
The following words, terms, and phrases, when used in this article, shall have the meanings ascribed to them in this section, except where the context clearly indicates a different meaning:
County means Forsyth County, a political subdivision of the State of Georgia.
Destination marketing organization means a private sector nonprofit organization or other private entity which is exempt from federal income tax under Section 501(c)(6) of the Internal Revenue Code of 1986 that is supported by the tax under this article, government budget allocations, private membership, or any combination thereof and the primary responsibilities of which are to encourage travelers to visit their destinations, encourage meetings and expositions in the area, and provide visitor assistance and support as needed. O.C.G.A. § 48-13-50.2(1).
Guestroom means a room occupied, or intended, arranged, or designed for occupancy by one or more occupants.
Hotel includes any hotel, motel, inn, lodge, tourist camp, tourist cabin, campground, or any other place in which room or rooms, lodgings, or accommodations are regularly furnished for value and shall apply to the furnishing for value of any room, lodging, or accommodation.
Innkeeper means:
(1) Any person that furnishes for value to the public any room or rooms, lodgings, or accommodations in a county or municipality and that is licensed by, or required to pay business or occupation taxes to, such municipality or county for operating a hotel, motel, inn, lodge, tourist camp, tourist cabin, campground, or any other place in which room or rooms, lodgings, or accommodations are regularly furnished for value.
(2) A marketplace facilitator who facilitates the furnishing for value to the public any guestrooms on behalf of another person in any manner, including, but not limited to, promoting, marketing, advertising, taking reservations, collecting payment, or as otherwise defined by O.C.G.A. § 48-13-50.2(2)(B).
Marketplace innkeeper means an innkeeper as defined in section 74-35 of this article, "innkeeper", subsection (2).
Occupancy means the use or possession, or the right to the use and possession, of any room or apartment in a hotel, or the right to the use or possession of the furnishings or to the services and accommodations accompanying the use and possession of the room.
Occupant means any person who, for a consideration, uses, possesses, or has the right to use or possess any room in a hotel under any lease, concession, permit, right of access, license to use, other agreement, or otherwise.
Permanent resident means any occupant as of a given date who has or shall have occupied or has or shall have the right of occupancy of any guestroom in a hotel for at least ten consecutive days next preceding such date.
Person includes any individual, firm, partnership, joint venture, association, social club, fraternal organization, joint stock company, corporation, non-profit corporation, limited liability company, cooperative nonprofit membership, estate, trust, business trust, receiver, trustee, syndicate, or any other group or combination acting as a unit, the plural as well as the singular number, excepting the United States of America, the State of Georgia, and any political subdivision of either thereof, upon which the county is without power to impose the tax provided for in this article.
Private sector nonprofit organization means a chamber of commerce, a convention and visitors bureau, a regional travel association, or any other private group organized for similar purposes which is exempt from federal income tax under Section 501(c)(6) of the Internal Revenue Code of 1986; provided, however, that a county or municipality which has prior to April 1, 1990, contracted for a required expenditure under applicable law with a private group which is exempt from federal income tax under provisions of Section 501(c) of the Internal Revenue Code other than Section 501(c)(6) may continue to contract for required expenditures with such a private group. O.C.G.A. § 48-13-50.2(3).
Promoting tourism, conventions, and trade shows means planning, conducting, or participating in programs of information and publicity designed to attract or advertise tourism, conventions, or trade shows. O.C.G.A. § 4813-50.2(4).
Rent means the consideration received for occupancy valued in money, whether received money or otherwise, including all receipts, cash, credit, and property or services of any kind or nature, and also the amount for which credit is allowed by the innkeeper to the occupant, without any deduction therefrom whatsoever.
Return means any return filed or required to be filed as provided in this article.
Tax refers to the tax imposed by this article.
Tourism product development means the expenditure of funds for the creation or expansion of physical attractions which are available and open to the public and which improve destination appeal to visitors, support visitors' experience, and are used by visitors. Such expenditures may include capital costs and operating expenses. Tourism product development may include: (A) Lodging for the public for no longer than 30 consecutive days to the same customer; (B) Overnight or short-term sites for recreational vehicles, trailers, campers, or tents; (C) Meeting, convention, exhibit, and public assembly facilities; (D) Sports stadiums, arenas, and complexes; (E) Golf courses associated with a resort development that are open to the general public on a contract or fee basis; (F) Racing facilities, including dragstrips, motorcycle racetracks, and auto or stock car racetracks or speedways; (G) Amusement centers, amusement parks, theme parks, or amusement piers; (H) Hunting preserves, trapping preserves, or fishing preserves or lakes; (I) Visitor information and welcome centers; (J) Wayfinding signage; (K) Permanent, nonmigrating carnivals or fairs; (L) Airplanes, helicopters, buses, vans, or boats for excursions or sightseeing; (M) Boat rentals, boat party fishing services, rowboat or canoe rentals, horse shows, natural wonder attractions, picnic grounds, river-rafting services, scenic railroads for amusement, aerial tramways, rodeos, water slides, or wave pools; (N) Museums, planetariums, art galleries, botanical gardens, aquariums, or zoological gardens; (O) Parks, trails, and other recreational facilities; or (P) Performing arts facilities.
(Ord. No. 86-C, § 1(Exh. A), 10-3-2024)
State Law reference— O.C.G.A. § 48-13-50.2(6).
997:
(1) Authority of county manager. The county manager or his/her designee shall administer and enforce the provision of this article.

998:
(1) Every innkeeper maintaining a place of business in unincorporated Forsyth County, as provided herein, and renting guestrooms in the county, and not otherwise exempted from this article, shall collect the tax imposed by this article at the time of collecting the rent from the occupant and, at the time of collecting the rent from the occupant give the occupant a receipt therefor. (Ord. No. 86-C, § 1(Exh. A), 10-3-2024)
999:
It shall be unlawful for any innkeeper to advertise or hold out or state to the public or to any guest, directly or indirectly, that the tax or any portion thereof will be assumed or absorbed by the innkeeper or that the tax will not be added to the rental of the guestroom, or that, if added, the tax or any portion thereof will be refunded.
(Ord. No. 86-C, § 1(Exh. A), 10-3-2024)
1000:
(1) Every person engaging or intending to engage within 60 days in business as an innkeeper in the county shall register with the county manager or his/her designee on a form provided by same. Failure to properly register with the county shall not relieve any person from the obligation of payment or collection of the tax after the date of imposition thereof.
(2) The registration form shall set forth the name under which such person transacts business or intends to transact business, the location of this place of business, the official address for the innkeeper to which notices required or allowed under this article shall be served, and such other information as the county manager or his/her designee may require which shall facilitate the collection of the tax. The registration shall be signed by the owner if a natural person, or, in the case of an entity other than a natural person, by an authorized officer, manager, member, or other person authorized to bind the entity and act on such entity's behalf. A separate registration shall be required for each place of business of an innkeeper. In the event any information supplied to the county manager or his/her designee on the registration shall become obsolete or shall not be accurate, it shall be the responsibility of the innkeeper to ensure that the registration is updated to reflect the current and correct information. The county manager or his/her designees shall, after such registration, issue without charge, a certificate of authority to each innkeeper to collect the tax from each occupant. Each certificate of authority shall be prominently displayed in the location of the business to which it is applicable so as to be seen and come readily to the notice of all occupants and persons seeking occupancy. The certificate of authority shall be nontransferable and non-assignable and shall be returned immediately to the county manager or his/her designee upon the cessation of business at the location named or upon the sale or transfer of the business at that location.
(Ord. No. 86-C, § 1(Exh. A), 10-3-2024)
1001:
(1) Due date of tax. All amounts collected as tax during any given month pursuant to this article shall be due and payable to Forsyth County on or before the 20th day of the following month (i.e., taxes collected for the month of March would be due on April 20). It is the intent of this part that the amount due and payable shall be submitted online, delivered in person, or postmarked on or before the 20th day of the month.
(2) Contents of return. The tax return filed with the county manager or his/her designee, shall provide information showing the gross rent, rent from permanent residents, taxable rent, the amount of tax collected or otherwise due for the month for which the return is submitted, and such other information as may be reasonably required.
(3) Collection fee allowed to innkeepers. Innkeepers collecting the tax shall be allowed a percentage of the tax due and accounted for as a collection fee and shall be reimbursed in the form of a deduction in submitting, reporting, and payment of the amount due to the county; provided, however, that innkeepers shall only be entitled to the collection fee in the event the payment of the amount due is not delinquent at the time of payment, as provided herein. The amount of the deduction or collection fee shall be three percent of the amount due.
(4) Extension for filing return and payment of tax. For good cause, to be determined in the sole discretion of the county manager or his/her designee, the county manager or his/her designee shall be authorized to extend, for a period of time not exceeding one month, the time for making any return or payment of tax. The county manager or his/her designee shall be authorized, however, to only extend the time for making any return or payment of tax once for any single return or payment. Any extension granted pursuant to this part shall be in writing and shall state the reason for the extension and the date upon which the extension shall terminate. Any person to whom an extension has been granted and who makes a return and pays the amount due as tax within the period of extension shall pay in addition to the tax interest on the amount of such tax outstanding at the rate of one percent per month, or fraction thereof, for the period commencing on the due date of said return and amount due to the date of actual payment of the amount due.
(Ord. No. 86-C, § 1(Exh. A), 10-3-2024)
1002:
(1) Re-computation of tax; authority; basis of re-computation. If the county manager or his/her designee is not satisfied with the return made by any person or the amount of the tax paid to the county by any person, the county manager or his/her designee is authorized to compute and determine the amount of tax required to be paid upon the basis of any known information.
(2) Interest on deficiency. The amount of the deficiency determination, exclusive of penalties, shall bear interest at the rate of one percent per month, or fraction thereof, from the due date of the tax as provided herein to the date of actual payment of the amount due (plus interest and penalties, if any).
(3) Offsetting overpayments. In making a deficiency determination, the county manager or his/her designee may offset any overpayments for prior returns against underpayments, penalties, and interest owing from another return. The interest on underpayments shall accrue as provided for interest on deficiency determinations as set forth herein.
(4) Penalty; negligence or disregard of rules and regulations. If any part of the deficiency for which a deficiency determination has been made is due to negligence on the part of any person or a disregard of this article or other authorized rules and regulations, a penalty equal to 15 percent of the amount of the deficiency shall be added to the total amount due for the deficiency.
(5) Penalty; fraud or intent to evade tax. If any part of the deficiency for which a deficiency determination has been made is due to fraud or an intent to evade any provisions of this article or other authorized rules and regulations, a penalty equal to 25 percent of the amount of the deficiency shall be added to the total amount due for the deficiency.
(6) Notice of county manager or his/her designee determination; service. The county manager or his/her designee shall give the innkeeper electronic or written notice of the deficiency determination, accrual of interest, and imposition of applicable penalties. The electronic notice shall be served to the email provided by the innkeeper, read receipt requested. The written notice shall be served personally or by certified mail, return receipt requested. If the written notice is served by certified mail, return receipt requested, the notice shall be addressed as the innkeeper's address appears on the last registration filed by the innkeeper pursuant to this article. In the case of service by written notice, service shall be deemed complete upon deposit of the certified mail in the United States post office.
(7) Time limit for notice of deficiency determination. Except in the case of fraud, intent to evade this article or authorized rules and regulations, or complete failure to make a return as required herein, every written notice of deficiency determination required by this article shall be served upon the innkeeper as provided herein within three years following either the date the tax was originally due or three years following the date upon which the return is actually filed, whichever shall last expire. There shall be no time limit for service of the written notice of deficiency determination for cases of fraud, intent to evade this article or authorized rules and regulations, or failure to make a return as required herein.
(Ord. No. 86-C, § 1(Exh. A), 10-3-2024)
1003:
(1) Estimation of gross receipts. If any person fails to make a return as required herein, the county manager or his/her designee shall make an estimate of the amount of the gross receipts of the person, or as the case may be, of the amount of the total rentals in the county which are subject to the tax. The estimate shall be made for all months in which the person failed to make the required return and shall be based upon any information in the county manager or his/her designee's possession. Upon the basis of this estimate, the county manager or his/her designee shall compute and determine the amount of tax required to be paid to the county, adding to the sum thus computed a penalty equal to 15 percent thereof.
(2) Offsets. In making an estimate determination where no required return is made, the county manager or his/her designee is authorized to offset overpayments made for any previous returns against the amount of tax due based on an estimate determination for any month during which no return was made.
(3) Interest. The amount of the tax due based on the estimate determination shall bear interest at the rate of one percent per month, or fraction thereof, commencing on the 20th day of the calendar month following the month during which no return was made and continuing until taxes due, plus interest and penalties thereon, are actually paid.
(4) Penalties for fraud or intent to evade. If the failure of any person to file a return is due to fraud or an intent to evade this article or duly authorized rules and regulations, a penalty equal to 25 percent of the amount of the tax due based on this estimate determination shall be added to the amount due for the monthly period for which no return was made. The penalty provided for in this part shall be in addition to and not in lieu of any other applicable penalties in this article.
(5) Notice. Promptly after making the estimate determination, the county manager or his/her designee shall notify the person failing to make the required return of the amount of tax due based on the estimate determination, plus the amount of accrued interest and penalties thereon. The notice shall be in writing and shall be served as provided in section 74-41(6) of this article.
(Ord. No. 86-C, § 1(Exh. A), 10-3-2024)
1004:
In the event any person properly files a timely return with the county manager or his/her designee as provided in section 74-40 of this article, but fails to pay the county the amount of tax on the due date as provided herein, the amount of tax shall bear interest at the rate of one percent per month, or fraction thereof, from the due date until the date the amount of tax, plus interest and penalties thereon, is paid. In addition, a penalty in the amount of 15 percent of the amount of the tax due shall be added to the amount due.
(Ord. No. 86-C, § 1(Exh. A), 10-3-2024)
1005:
(1) Action for delinquent tax. Except in the case of fraud, intent to evade this article or authorized rules and regulations, or failure to file a return as required herein, at any time within three years after any amount of tax required to be collected becomes due and payable and at any time within three years after the delinquency of any amount of tax required to be collected, the county manager or his/her designee may bring an action in any court of competent jurisdiction in the name of the county to collect the delinquent amount together with interest and penalties as provided in this article, court fees, filing fees, attorney's fees, and other fees and costs incident thereto. There shall be no time limit for bringing an action as provided herein in cases of fraud, intent to evade this article or authorized rules and regulations, or failure to make a return as required herein.
(2) Duty of successors and assigns of innkeeper to withhold tax. If any innkeeper liable for any amount under this article sells, transfers, assigns, releases, quit-claims, or conveys any business operation which is subject to the tax, the innkeeper's successors and/or assigns shall withhold a sufficient amount from the purchase price of the business operation to cover any amounts which may be due as tax until the innkeeper produces a receipt from the county manager or his/her designee stating that the tax due has been paid or that no tax is due. In the event the successors and/or assigns of the innkeeper fail to withhold a sufficient amount from the purchase price of the business operation to cover any amounts which may be due as tax, the successors and/or assigns shall be liable for the amount of tax which is due. If any innkeeper quits, closes, or stops operating the business which is subject to the tax for any reason, the successors, heirs, and/or assigns of the innkeeper shall remain liable for any amounts which may be due as tax.
(3) Tax credit for interest paid or erroneously or illegally collected. Whenever the amount of any tax, interest, or penalty has been paid more than once, or has been erroneously or illegally collected or received by the county under this article, it may be offset by the county manager or his/her designee. If the innkeeper or marketplace innkeeper determines that there has been an overpayment or multiple payments, which fact has not been determined by the county manager or his/her designee, such innkeeper or marketplace innkeeper shall have a period of three years from the date of payment to file a claim with the county, in writing, stating the specific grounds upon which the claim is founded. The claim shall then be audited. If the claim is approved, the excess amount paid to the county may be credited on any amounts then due and payable from the innkeeper or marketplace innkeeper, or the county manager or his/her designee is authorized to refund the amount to the innkeeper or marketplace innkeeper. Notwithstanding anything contained in this section, no innkeeper or marketplace innkeeper shall have any right to file a claim for overpayment in the event that alleged overpayment is a result of an estimated determination as provided in section 74-42 of this article.
(Ord. No. 86-C, § 1(Exh. A), 10-3-2024)
1006:
Notwithstanding any other penalties imposed herein, any person violating the provisions of this article shall be deemed to be guilty of a misdemeanor and upon conviction thereof, shall be punished by fine not exceeding $1,000.00, imprisonment for up to six months, or both. Each day during which a violation of this article is committed, continued, or permitted shall constitute a separate offense. Any innkeeper or marketplace innkeeper who fails to register as required herein, fails, or refuses to furnish any necessary returns, fails, or refuses to furnish a supplemental return or other data reasonably required by the county manager or his/her designee, or who renders a false or fraudulent return shall be deemed guilty of an offense and, upon conviction thereof, shall be punished as described herein.
(Ord. No. 86-C, § 1(Exh. A), 10-3-2024)
1007:
(1) The revenue from the tax imposed by this article shall be allocated in accordance with the requirements of O.C.G.A. § 48-13-51(b)(5) and O.C.G.A. § 48-13-51(b)(6) and as further provided in this section 74-46.
(2) In accordance with O.C.G.A. § 48-13-51(b)(5)(A), in each fiscal year during which a tax is collected under this article, an amount equal to not less than 50 percent of the total amount of taxes collected that exceed the amount of taxes that would be collected at the rate of five percent shall be expended for promoting tourism, conventions, and trade shows by the destination marketing organization designated by the county.

(4) In accordance with O.C.G.A. § 48-13-51(b)(6), an amount equal to the amount of taxes that would have been collected at a rate of five percent shall be expended in accordance with O.C.G.A. § 48-13-51(a)(3). Of such amount, no less than an amount equal to the amount of taxes that would have been collected at a rate of two percent shall be expended for promoting tourism, conventions, and trade shows through contracts with a private sector nonprofit organization or other authorized entity under O.C.G.A. § 48-13-51(a)(3). The remaining amount of taxes that would have been collected at a rate of five percent which are not otherwise expended for promoting tourism, conventions, and trade shows may be expended for the provision of other local government services.
(Ord. No. 86-C, § 1(Exh. A), 10-3-2024)
1010:
As used in this article, the terms: "dealer;" "energy;" "local sales" and "use tax"; and "purchaser" shall have the same meanings as provided in O.C.G.A. § 48-13-110.
(Ord. No. 119, § 1, 12-20-2012, eff. 1-1-2013)
1011:
In accordance with the provisions of O.C.G.A. § 48-13-110 et seq., there is imposed within the territorial limits of the special district created pursuant to O.C.G.A. § 48-13-111, an excise tax on the sale, use, storage, or consumption of energy when such sale, use, storage, or consumption would have constituted a taxable event for purposes of sales and use tax under O.C.G.A. § 48-8-1 et seq. but for the exemption in O.C.G.A. § 48-8-3.2.
(Ord. No. 119, § 2, 12-20-2012, eff. 1-1-2013)
1012:
(a) Such excise tax shall be levied and collected by the governing authority of Forsyth County pursuant to O.C.G.A. §§ 48-13-112 and 48-13-114 and as provided in this section.
(b) Except as otherwise provided in this section, the rate of such excise tax shall be phased in, pursuant to O.C.G.A. § 48-13-112, over a four-year period as follows:
(1) For the period commencing January 1, 2013, and concluding at the last moment of December 31, 2013, such excise tax shall be at a rate equivalent to 25 percent of the total amount of local sales and use tax in effect in such special district that would be collected on the sale, use, storage, or consumption of energy but for the exemption in O.C.G.A. § 48-8-3.2;
(2) For the period commencing January 1, 2014, and concluding at the last moment of December 31, 2014, such excise tax shall be at a rate equivalent to 50 percent of the total amount of local sales and use tax in effect in such special district that would be collected on the sale, use, storage, or consumption of energy but for the exemption in O.C.G.A. § 48-8-3.2;
(3) For the period commencing January 1, 2015, and concluding at the last moment of December 31, 2015, such excise tax shall be at a rate equivalent to 75 percent of the total amount of local sales and use tax in effect in such special district that would be collected on the sale, use, storage, or consumption of energy but for the exemption in O.C.G.A. § 48-8-3.2; and
(4) On or after January 1, 2016, such excise tax shall be at a rate equivalent to 100 percent of the total amount of local sales and use tax in effect in such special district that would be collected on the sale, use, storage, or consumption of energy but for the exemption in O.C.G.A. § 48-8-3.2.
(c) In accordance with O.C.G.A. § 48-8-3.2(c)(4), if a competitive project of regional significance under O.C.G.A. § 48-8-3(92) is started in the special district, it shall not be subject to the phase-in period contained in subsections (b)(1), (2), and (3) of this section, and the sale, use, storage, or consumption of energy in connection therewith shall be subject to the rate specified in subsection (b)(4) of this section notwithstanding the January 1, 2016 limitation in subsection (b)(4).
(d) Following such initial imposition during the phase-in time period, on and after January 1, 2016, the rate of the excise tax levied and collected by the governing authority of Forsyth County shall be directed by O.C.G.A. § 48-13-112(d).
(1) Such rate shall be controlled by the maximum amount of local sales and use tax in effect in the special district, but in no event more than two percent (except in the case where the municipal option water and sewer tax is levied, in which case that rate shall not exceed three percent).
(2) In the event the total rate of local sales and use taxes in effect in the special district decreases from two percent to one percent, the rate of the excise tax under this ordinance shall likewise be reduced at the same time such local sales and use tax rate reduction becomes effective.
(3) In the event the total rate of local sales and use taxes in effect in the special district increases from one percent to two percent, the rate of the excise tax under this ordinance shall likewise be increased at the same time such local sales and use tax rate increase becomes effective.
(Ord. No. 119, § 3, 12-20-2012, eff. 1-1-2013)
1014:
(a) The governing authority of Forsyth County, or the collecting officer appointed under section 74-68 of this article, shall make diligent efforts to identify all energy providers and purchasers in the special district and to ascertain whether such a purchaser has completed a uniform exemption certificate provided from the website of the Georgia Department of Revenue seeking to qualify such purchaser for the exemption under O.C.G.A. § 48-8-3.2. Such certificate shall be utilized by such governing authority or collecting officer for the purpose of determining the applicability of the excise tax under this article.
(b) An energy provider shall be authorized to rely upon such uniform exemption certificates. No penalty shall attach to such provider for failure to collect the excise tax under this ordinance when it has properly collected and remitted local sales and use taxes on such energy where the purchaser would have qualified for the uniform exemption certificate but failed to apply for such certificate or where the purchaser received such certificate but failed to file it with the energy provider.
(Ord. No. 119, § 5, 12-20-2012, eff. 1-1-2013)
1015:
The excise tax imposed pursuant to this ordinance shall become effective on January 1, 2013, and shall be due and payable to the governing authority of Forsyth County monthly on or before the twentieth (20 th ) day of the month following each respective month in which such taxes are collected, and payment shall be accompanied by a return for the preceding monthly period showing the gross sales and purchases arising from all sales and purchases taxable under this article during the preceding calendar month.
(Ord. No. 119, § 6, 12-20-2012, eff. 1-1-2013)
1016:
(a) Pursuant to O.C.G.A. § 48-13-114(b), the excise tax proceeds shall be allocated and distributed by the governing authority of Forsyth County at the end of each calendar month. A lift axle may not be used in computing the maximum total gross weight authorized for any vehicle or load under this paragraph.
(c) No wheel on any vehicle operated upon any public road maintained by the county, equipped with high pressure, pneumatic solid rubber or cushion tires shall carry a load which exceeds 8,000 pounds by more than 13 percent, or an axle load which exceeds 16,000 pounds by more than 13 percent; no wheel equipped with low pressure pneumatic tires shall carry a load which exceeds 9,000 pounds by more than 13 percent, or any axle load which exceeds 18,000 pounds by more than 13 percent; an axle load shall be defined as the total load on all wheels whose centers may be included between two parallel transverse vertical planes 40 inches apart. If the driver of any vehicle can comply with the requirements of this section by shifting or equalizing the load on all wheels or axles and does so when requested by the proper authority, said driver shall not be operating in violation of this section.
(d) Any person driving or in charge or control of any of the restricted vehicles defined in the preceding section when upon streets other than those designated as truck routes, shall be prepared to present for the inspection of law enforcement officers his log book, weight slips, delivery slips or other written evidence of his destination and point of origin to justify the presence of the restricted vehicle on a street other than a designated truck route. (a) The purpose of this article is to provide protection to the citizens of the county by ensuring that water distribution systems are adequate for fire protection, are sanitary, and are of sufficient size and quality to receive public water service as such becomes available. It is necessary to ensure that distribution systems are sufficient to become part of a wider distribution network than that existing at the time of installation. It is also necessary to consider water pressure variations resulting from elevation differentials within the county, the need to minimize water losses, and the need to minimize maintenance costs.
(b) This article shall apply to each and every water line installed below ground level in the unincorporated area of the county; provided, however, this article shall not apply to a water line installed by the owner of real property on his own property from a water source and serving not more than three dwelling units, or serving not more than two commercial or business establishments, or serving agricultural activities; and provided, further, that this exception shall not be available in any case where any portion of the water line is to be laid linearly within a public right-of-way, or a right-of-way required to be dedicated to the county under any ordinance, resolution, or other regulation.
(c) This article is passed with the specific knowledge that it contains standards more stringent than underground system installation standards present in the plumbing code now in effect. It is specifically the intention of this article to impose such more stringent standards, and subsequent amendments to plumbing codes now in effect, or adoption of other plumbing codes, shall in no way modify the standards of this article unless specifically stated in any such codes adopted in this article.
(Ord. No. 13, ch. 2, 8-22-1983)
